quest.title: For the Same Land
quest.description: After the routing of the black sun that had hung high in the sky, Natlan finally had a precious moment of respite. You decide to go help the Flower-Feather Clan, which had been hit hardest by the calamity, with their reconstruction efforts...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Primogem x30, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

dialogues.speaker: Yopia
dialogues.text: I brought all the stuff over, Coach. What's next?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Just take it easy before the real work begins.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: You two are in charge of repairing the houses to the north. The rest of you should go west. The road practically crumbled beneath my feet on my way here — the whole thing will need to be reinforced.

dialogues.speaker: Matlan
dialogues.text: Alright! I'll start by moving the boxes over.

dialogues.speaker: Hueliyo
dialogues.text: I'll help you. These things can get pretty heavy.

dialogues.speaker: Matlan
dialogues.text: No, no... I got this. These muscles aren't just for show, you know. See that? Perfectly defined! I can lift this stuff up with one hand!

dialogues.speaker: Hueliyo
dialogues.text: Fine, as long as you don't wind up too sore to move tomorrow. I don't want to hear any complaints from you!

dialogues.speaker: Matlan
dialogues.text: Just prepare to be amazed... *heave*

dialogues.speaker: Matlan
dialogues.text: Aah, my back...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Well, what doesn't kill you makes you stronger... Take him to get some rest and apply some meds.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: And you, take it easy for the next few days, alright? I don't want this getting worse, and don't push yourself. You can help out once you're better.

dialogues.speaker: Matlan
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I knew I should've trained harder...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Working out is different from real work. You gotta ease into it... Anyone not having an assignment? Chief Mutota needs our help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Iansan!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Paimon! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were just about to ask you the same thing! We didn't expect to run into you in these parts.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Well, my tribe's in pretty good shape, all things considered — we're already done with all the repairs. I heard the Flower-Feather Clan was hit a lot worse, though, so I decided to come help.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: On the way, I ran into a caravan of merchants from my tribe and brought them along. These are my students.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Oh, I didn't tell you before?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: I'm a professional trainer. I design workout plans, meal plans, all that good stuff. If you're interested in a particular sport, I'm happy to whip you into shape!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Anyway, that's enough idle talk for now. A little while earlier, the chief asked me to bring a few people to help with something.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Are you two free? As you can see, due to... unforeseen circumstances, I'm short a few people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course, we're also here to help! Let's go see the chief.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Perfect! Then follow me.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Haha, good memory! You a sports lover? I can design a training plan for you!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Looks like you're in pretty good shape already. Competitive fighting, extreme sports — you could take your pick! As for you, Paimon... We might have to start you off on a balanced meal plan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What!? There's nothing wrong about Paimon's current meal plan! Like today, Paimon just had some Blazed Meat Stew, Fried Shrimp Beanballs, Sour Sauce Ceviche, and Stuffed N' Mashed Potatoes... That's practically nothing!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Uhhh, this case sounds even worse than I imagined... Oh, I know just the thing — kale juice! I'll make you some soon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Kale juice... Wait! Isn't that your favorite drink, {NICKNAME}? If Iansan's going to make some for free, Paimon would feel terrible if you won't get to try it...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Let's just get straight to the point. Are the people behind you warriors from your tribe? Did something bad happen to them?

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Cold... So cold. Duarte, are you there?

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: I'm drowning... And there's something in the water...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's on the ground, but it almost looks like he's trying to... swim?

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: Hehehe...

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: The Abyss... The Abyss is coming...

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: There are eyes in my hands, and hands in my stomach, and my stomach is full of teeth... It ate all of you. It's coming for me, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, we haven't been eaten. We're right here!

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: Monstrous beasts! How did you get in here!?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: *sigh* As you can see, their mental state is quite poor.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: They went missing after the battle. We found them in the wilderness in the days that followed, but the damage had already been done...

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: We found them unconscious in areas corrupted by Abyssal Tumors, lying next to their deceased comrades. My only guess is that something terrible must have happened during the battle...

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: According to the chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind, sudden exposure to a large amount of Abyssal power can have mental as well as physical repercussions.

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: We've never seen the effects this heightened before, but maybe Gosoythoth was just too powerful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gosoythoth? What's that?

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: It's the Abyssal monster that appeared in the sky not too long ago. After consulting our ancient legends, we decided to call it Gosoythoth, "Reaper of the Abyss."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that giant black ball! Didn't we force it to retreat, though?

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: True, it poses no threat to us now, but whatever wound it inflicted on these warriors still endures. We scoured all sorts of records for a solution, but... nothing came of it.

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: There was some mention of a treatment from several hundred years ago, but that knowledge is long gone...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I could try to help?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, you can purify Abyssal power! Might as well give it a try!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You try to purify the Abyssal power within them, but their mental state appears unchanged.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It... It didn't work?

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: That must mean purifying the Abyssal power within them still isn't enough... In any case, thank you for trying.

response.speaker: Izcalli
response.text: So, what can we do now? Don't tell me... My friend is just going to be like this forever?

response.speaker: Cuallee
response.text: Come back to me, Cochitta! Please, don't leave me like this...

response.speaker: Utsil
response.text: We beat Gosoythoth... They survived the battle! Are we really just gonna sit back and watch them lose their minds?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Of course not.

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: What is it, Iansan?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: We'll take it case by case. First of all, we shouldn't keep them cooped up in here. The environment isn't doing them any good.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: #Let them go where they feel comfortable, and {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and I will talk to them.

response.speaker: Ticitl
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Utsil
response.text: Are you sure about this?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: I know you're worried, but we don't have any other solution, right? Maybe it works, maybe it doesn't... But, we won't know until we try.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Well? Don't just stand there — let them go. Send someone to follow them, but don't stick too close. We just need to keep tabs on them.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Following Iansan's command, the crowd disperses.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Alright, it's up to us now. Let's talk to them one by one.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: This is a bad situation, but I know the warriors will find a way to pull through. After all, we've overcome so many challenges already, what's one more?

talks.objective: Talk to the first afflicted individual

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: *sobbing*

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Found him... Hello, can you hear me?

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: So dark... So cold... I want to go home...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Okay! Just wait a little longer, and we'll take you home.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: The caravan from my tribe should have brought some firewood... I think starting a bonfire might help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: When it's dark, damp, and cold, what's better than a fire?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Maybe the light and warmth will help change what he sees... Wait here while I grab some firewood.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You light a bonfire...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Light... Underwater? Where is it coming from?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's working!

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Is someone there? Please save me... No, wait, you have to leave this place! The water's too deep! You won't make it!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: It's okay, we brought some friends from the People of the Springs. They're great swimmers! We're here to save you.

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: No... Please... Just leave me...

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Duarte...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, it's not working anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Looks like the bonfire wasn't enough.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: That was the second time he mentioned the name "Duarte"... Maybe we can start there. Let's ask around and see what we can learn.

dialogues.speaker: Izcalli
dialogues.text: My friend... Is he any better?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: We're working on it, but I wanted to ask... Does the name "Duarte" ring any bells for you?

dialogues.speaker: Izcalli
dialogues.text: Duarte? Oh yeah, I remember...

dialogues.speaker: Izcalli
dialogues.text: Duarte was the name of Atoco's saurian companion. Atoco almost drowned as a child, and Duarte was the one who saved him.

dialogues.speaker: Izcalli
dialogues.text: He dove deep into the water and used all his strength to carry Atoco back to the surface. It was pretty touch and go, but both of them made it in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: That means we just need to bring Duarte here, and—

dialogues.speaker: Izcalli
dialogues.text: Well, you see... Duarte died four years ago during an Abyss invasion. He was helping evacuate injured warriors from the front lines, but fell to an ambush.

choices.text: ...Maybe we don't need the real Duarte.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what do you mean?

response.speaker: Izcalli
response.text: You're right... Duarte didn't have many distinguishing features. I don't think he ever stood out next to the others.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We just need to impersonate him.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Based on the look on your face, I'm guessing you already have a plan.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Alright, let's get to work... Oh, and thank you for the information. We'll do whatever we can to help your friend.

response.speaker: Izcalli
response.text: No problem. Thank you for looking out for him.

response.speaker: Izcalli
response.text: He was a bit on the smaller side, but other than that, he was just your average Qucusaur.

response.speaker: Izcalli
response.text: Hold on, what are you planning?

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: No, wait... I failed... I...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Oh no, he's getting suspicious.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Slam him hard)

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: *violent coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: *panting* Duarte...! Wait, you're not Duarte...

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: How did I get here? Who are you people...

dialogues.speaker: Izcalli
dialogues.text: Atoco!

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Izcalli? What's going on? All I remember is the battle against the Abyss, and then... I was drowning, and a saurian that looked like Duarte saved me. How did I get here?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain the situation to Atoco.

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: You went through all that for me? While all I did was to cause trouble for everyone. I'm so sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: None of this is your fault. Maybe it's not my place to say this, but... Go easy on yourself. You deserve to move past what happened here... and what happened to Duarte.

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Th—Thank you... I appreciate that.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Go on, get some rest. Izcalli, we'll leave him to you.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: We made it, Chief.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: #Iansan, {NICKNAME}, Paimon — I'm so glad you're here.

talks.objective: Talk to the second afflicted individual

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: It's coming for me... It's gonna eat me...!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: It's okay, there's nothing to fear. Gosoythoth has lost. Nothing can hurt you anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: It's no use. It'll just come back... Nothing can stop it. Nothing can stop the Abyss!

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: It will devour everyone. Heh... One day, we'll all be reunited in the pit of its stomach.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe it's just Paimon, but she seems to be in even worse shape than Atoco.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She can talk to us, but nothing she says makes any sense. She also seems really afraid...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Afraid... is right.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I wonder what triggered it... The battle against the Abyss? Or maybe, like Atoco, it's some deep-rooted fear, and the Abyss just made it worse.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Alright, just like before — let's go see what we can learn about her past.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Iansan, I heard you cured Atoco! I'm so relieved... Is there anything I can do to help? If you need extra hands, I can—

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Chief Mutota! Perfect timing, I was just looking for you. I wanted to ask you some questions...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain what you did to cure Atoco as you take Chief Mutota to a more secluded place to talk.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: I think you're on to something... The mental distress does seem to be connected to pre-existing fears and anxieties.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Cochitta doesn't like it when people talk about her past, but the situation is urgent, so I guess I'll be the bad guy.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Iansan, do you believe there are people in this world destined for battle?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Yes, I get that feeling sometimes when I'm instructing a particularly gifted student. It's something like... "wow, you were born to play this sport."

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Then, what about people destined to be unfit for battle?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: When Cochitta was little, her parents died fighting the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: She was only eleven or twelve at the time, and her brother even younger still. The two saw their parents collapse in a pool of blood as flames roared and spread all around them...

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Cochitta trained hard to become a warrior, but still found fighting abyss monsters too difficult to handle. She and her brother were left with severe trauma after the incident, pain and fear that they could not get over no matter what.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, isn't Cochitta one of the warriors who fought the Abyss? Didn't you find her unconscious out on the field?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Yes, we did. You see, something changed within her several years ago when the Abyss attacked our tribe, and broke into her home.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: By the time the guards rushed to the scene, they found her standing there, weapon outstretched, hands trembling, her brother huddling behind her for safety...

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: And the Abyss monster dead at her feet. She didn't even look at it, and just kept repeating the same thing over and over — "you're the only family I have left. I won't let anything happen to you."

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: She became a completely different person after that. She earned a reputation as a very capable warrior, and fought countless battles against the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: We all thought she overcame the trauma, and we were so happy for her, but now it seems like even if she buried it deep within herself, the fear still never left her.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Maybe fighting the Abyss was her way of making sure she wouldn't lose anyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Maybe the thought of experiencing that pain again scared her more than the Abyss. On the outside, her choice to fight made her seem strong, but she never forgot the trauma of that night... The Abyss just brought it back to the surface.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can we help her?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: This one is tricky. If we can find the right opportunity, then—

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Cuallee?

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: Cuallee... What are you doing with that weapon?

dialogues.speaker: Cuallee
dialogues.text: Show me the monster that hurt you!

dialogues.speaker: Cuallee
dialogues.text: I'll make it pay! I... I'm gonna protect you this time!

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Calm down, Cuallee. That monster is already—

dialogues.speaker: Cuallee
dialogues.text: I can do it! I don't care what it takes! I just want her to get better... She is the only family I have left!

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: Family...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Hold on, Chief Mutota. Looks like Cochitta is responding to his words.

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: If Cuallee goes to battle... the Abyss will devour him...

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: I can't let that happen. I have to do something...

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: But, it's useless. No one can beat the Abyss. It's a death sentence, just like what happened to Mom and Dad...

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: But I'm no warrior... I'm just a coward. Still... I have to protect Cuallee. What should I do?

response.speaker: Cuallee
response.text: Cochitta...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think you just need to fight it one more time.

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: Fight it... one more time?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: #Good idea, {NICKNAME}... Her fear of the Abyss runs deep, but she still has the will to fight.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: She just needs to defeat an Abyss monster by herself, and we can prove to her that the Abyss isn't indestructible, just like you said!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: I think it's worth a try. Plus, with us around, we can make sure she won't get hurt. Although, that also means finding an Abyss monster...

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: Try checking the mountains to the north. A few fled in that direction after the battle.

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: I dispatched a team to clear them out, so most of them should be gone. But, there might still be a few stragglers.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Great! Then let's go right now. Cochitta, think you can make it?

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: There's no turning back. I have to face it, even if it will devour me whole...

response.speaker: Cuallee
response.text: I'm coming, too! I'm not letting my sister face this alone! Not anymore!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Alright, then stick close. Let's go!

talks.objective: Search for the remaining Abyss monsters

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Found 'em... Let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Everything alright, Cochitta? You don't have to force yourself to do this.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: How can we make this easier for her...? I guess we could wear them down first, but I think it's better to stand guard for now. We should wait for the right moment to intervene.

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: You...! You were the ones who killed them...!

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: (As a kid, I thought my parents were invincible. They were always so strong and gentle... They seemed like the most powerful people in the world.)

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: (But, I can still see the image of them collapsed at my feet that night — the raging fire, the smoke, the smell of blood, the sound of my brother's cries... It's all burned into my brain.)

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: (They told me to run, and I could see the fear in their eyes. I've been running from my fears ever since.)

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: (But, why didn't my parents run? It must have been because—)

dialogues.speaker: Cuallee
dialogues.text: You can do it!

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: (...Because of our family. When you have someone to protect, there's no backing down, no matter what.)

dialogues.speaker: Utsil
dialogues.text: *sigh* Looks like he's not going anywhere. I don't know why, but he's looking at us with such... hatred.

dialogues.speaker: Utsil
dialogues.text: Anyway, please don't let me keep you. I'll stay here and keep an eye on him.

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: Where are the rest? Where are they hiding?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: That last strike was absolute perfection! You pulverized them in a single hit.

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: That's impossible... They were gigantic beasts, crawling with eyes, ready to devour everything in sight...

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: No, wait... What am I saying? Abyss monsters are not actually that scary... I've defeated them before. I know I have...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's back to normal!

response.speaker: Cuallee
response.text: Cochitta!

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: What just happened?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You explain the situation to Cochitta.

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: That is... quite embarrassing. Sorry about that.

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: I've always envied warriors who don't get scared or feel lost. It really felt like I was getting stronger over the years, but in the end, maybe I never made any progress at all...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: It's important to listen to your limits. Just like in training, pushing too hard will only hurt you in the long run. Everyone needs time to rest.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Besides, I have a feeling you won't have to face those fears alone anymore.

response.speaker: Cuallee
response.text: Even though we're both scared of monsters, you were always the one who stepped up to protect me, but not anymore. I'm gonna get stronger. From now on, we're in this together!

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: Is that so? Then I'll look forward to the day when you'll be all big and formidable.

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: I finally feel like myself again, and I couldn't have done it without you all. Thank you for everything.

response.speaker: Cochitta
response.text: I think I'll rest here for a bit. I don't think I can make it back to the tribe just yet...

response.speaker: Cuallee
response.text: I'll keep you company!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Alright, then we'll head back. I made sure to check the surrounding area for monsters, and it's all clear, so take your time.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Sometimes, our fears never truly leave us. But, tomorrow's a new day. As long as you keep moving forward, there will be better days to come.

dialogues.speaker: Ohtli
dialogues.text: Atoco's all better! Did you hear?

dialogues.speaker: Itotia
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Ohtli
dialogues.text: #Yes, really! It's all thanks to {NICKNAME} and Iansan.

dialogues.speaker: Itotia
dialogues.text: #I see... I was wondering why {NICKNAME} was chosen to accompany the Pyro Archon in the final battle, but I guess {F#s}he really can do the impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Let out a low roar)

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: You sense it, don't you? This place is dangerous...

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Still, hahaha... Hearing you make that noise reminds me of our first few battles together. You were such a little thing back then, and I also had no idea what I was doing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He's still trapped in the hallucination.)

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: #That's two people down! You're an amazing problem-solver, {NICKNAME}! Probably a well-honed skill from all your travels, right?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: You really know how to give people hope! Ever since you came to Natlan, I've been feeling a lot better about our chances of winning this war!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Honestly, Paimon was at a complete loss when she saw so many sick people on the hot-air balloon platform.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We only found a solution this time because you kept your cool and took control of the situation. You deserve most of the credit!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Haha, well, who am I to turn down such a nice compliment!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Most people say the first step is the hardest. But, it's not actually all that hard. Exaggerating the difficulty in your own head is where the fear comes in.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: "I'll never get it," or "Might as well not try"... I hear that kind of talk all the time. But, if you break your goal into smaller parts, the first steps might actually turn out to be the easiest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, you're right! That makes a lot of sense...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Just like when I told you to eat less meat and drink more kale juice.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: You probably heard that and thought... "I can never eat meat again. I have to drink kale juice for every meal. I'll practically starve..."

choices.text: That's why Paimon was so against it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee-hee...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: In reality, all it takes to start is eating two fewer servings of Blazed Meat Stew and adding some kale juice for nutrition. That's it! It's not about making drastic changes all at once.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds like something Paimon could do! But, would that really change anything?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Consistency is key! You can't accomplish your goals in one fell swoop. You have to eat away at them little by little.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: My Ancient Name means "power," did you know that? So, everyone thought I would grow up to be this tall, burly, muscular warrior.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: But, that's not what happened. A lot of people were confused and disappointed. My fellow warriors couldn't understand why I inherited that name over them.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: At first, I also felt lost. It was only later that I realized true strength basically boils down to problem-solving. Physical strength is just a means to an end like everything else.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: So, I began to break problems down into smaller parts. When facing an impossible situation, you just need to act. And if you fail, so what? That's just life.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Anyway, that's what I've learned over the years. Maybe it'll come in handy for you some day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When you put it that way, Paimon's almost encouraged to start drinking kale juice tomorrow... No, today! Paimon will start today!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're amazing, Iansan! You really make Paimon feel like she can do the impossible! Maybe your true strength is giving other people strength...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: I don't deserve that much credit!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: You already have that strength within you. I'm sure you've faced more obstacles than I can imagine during your travels. But, you never gave up! That proves it!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: I bet I could learn a thing or two from you.

response.speaker: Utsil
response.text: Iansan! Bad news! Ocotlan is out of control!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Stay calm! I'll be right there!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Looks like the time for conversation is over. C'mon, let's go see him.

choices.text: I'd probably feel the same way...
You got them through the initial stage of panic.

dialogues.speaker: Utsil
dialogues.text: What are you doing, Ocotlan? Wake up!

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: Don't you recognize us, my boy?

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: (The Abyss monsters are everywhere... everywhere...)

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: (They've taken over the tribe. No corner is safe...)

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: (Did we lose the battle? No... It's pointless to think about that now. A warrior only has one job — fight until the very end.)

dialogues.speaker: Utsil
dialogues.text: Careful! He's not himself!

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: Ocotlan!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Get back!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I don't think he can hear us right now.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: We need to get him under control. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: Please, son. You've got to stop... You can't keep going like this.

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: Wretched... monsters...

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: Give me my family back!

dialogues.speaker: Utsil
dialogues.text: Look, Ocotlan! That's your father! He's standing right in front of you!

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: Get out of my home! I'll never forgive you!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you alright, sir?

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: *coughing*... I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: Please, don't hurt my son. He's... Just trying to protect his home...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Don't worry. We'll figure something out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... But, what should we do now? He's different from the other two. It's like he can't hear us at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He keeps calling us monsters... We're basically enemies to him now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And he sure knows how to fight.

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: Ocotlan...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: He has a fighting spirit, that's for sure. But, we can't keep him unconscious forever. I need to think...
...Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome.
...Five hundred years later, and it's resurfaced again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That voice, it's—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Captain!?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: So, you've seen this illness before?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Direct contact with high concentrations of Abyssal power causes irreversible mental trauma in most people.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: The exact presentation will vary according to trauma level. Some will suffer from superficial hallucinations and maintain the capacity to perceive the outside world. In such cases, verbal and physical interaction can be used to break through the hallucination.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: However, there are also those who are so far gone, entrenched in hallucinations so deep, that medical intervention is the only option. That's why we developed the Draught of Lucidity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Draught of... Lucidity?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: It's a kind of medicine that can dispel the psychological impact of the Abyss. The treatment comes with severe side-effects, including chronic migraines for the rest of the patient's life, so it's reserved for the worst cases.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: This man is a devoted warrior, one not easily swayed from battle. That is precisely why it's so difficult to pull him out of this hallucination.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: If you trust me to be true to my word, give him this.

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: Wretched monsters... Setting up an ambush...

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: Give me your worst! It's either your end or mine!

dialogues.speaker: Utsil
dialogues.text: Hurry! He's awake!

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: Please, give him the draught. My son thinks he's alone in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: In his mind, all his family and comrades are gone, and only enemies remain... There's nothing more painful for a warrior than losing everything you've fought so hard to protect.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: At the father's request, Iansan accepts the draught from The Captain and quickly gives it to Ocotlan.

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: Monsters... Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: What's going on? I... Dad? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Ocotlan
dialogues.text: My head hurts... I just had the strangest dream. I dreamt the Abyss took over the tribe...

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: It's alright, my boy... It was just a nightmare.

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: Let's go home. You need a good night's sleep. Ah, but first — I want to thank you for saving my son. May I ask your name?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Th... *ahem* Just "Capitano" is fine.

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: I owe you more than words can say, Mr. Capitano. My name is Munay. You're welcome in my home any time.

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: Time to go, son. Can you stand?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: #I'll help you carry him back. {NICKNAME}, let's meet up later.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After the crowd disperses, The Captain hands a few more doses of medicine to the guards, so that the remaining warriors can be cured.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thank goodness everything turned out alright.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Think nothing of it. I agreed to offer you my aid, so this is merely a part of that duty.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Besides... I care deeply about this land.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! When we were with Mavuika, you told us you and your soldiers defended Natlan against the Abyss five hundred years ago.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: That's right. My desire to protect this nation remains unchanged.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: When my platoon arrived in Natlan five hundred years ago, like you, we were true outlanders. But, as time passed, I encountered the people of this land and witnessed their desperate struggle against the Abyss.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Though many of the warriors were rash and inexperienced, they were steadfast and fearless in battle, willing to do anything to protect their fellow citizens... oftentimes with complete disregard for their own survival.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Just as I fought for the glory of Khaenri'ah, they fought for the survival of their nation. We happened to share a common enemy, so I decided to offer my aid.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: We fought side by side to the very end. I traveled to many places after that, but I never forgot this land. Even now... My work in Natlan remains unfinished.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: They remember who I used to be — the "Sentinel Knight" who fought with the Masters of the Night-Wind. Still, I prefer to leave all that in the past.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: That name carries with it the glory of my homeland and the honor of Natlan. Yet, I failed to bring my soldiers home, and I failed to help Natlan defeat the Abyss.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, that's not your fault! The Abyss is way stronger than any of us imagined...

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: You need not comfort me. I am no longer who I once was... Let the events of the past continue to collect dust in the annals of history. I will continue to help Natlan in my own way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Like with the Draught of Lucidity?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who knew you could make medicine! Were you a doctor before?

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: The draught was Guthred's invention. He was a respected military doctor as well as my trusted second-in-command.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: We faced a similar situation to what you witnessed today. The endless battles against the Abyss triggered delusions among the soldiers, to the point where some attempted to kill each other.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: In order to develop a treatment as fast as possible, Guthred used himself as a test subject. He passed away shortly after the draught was complete.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: That's who he was — unrelenting in his pursuits, no matter the cost, no matter the sacrifice... in the end, he even gave himself up for a chance at success.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I'm sure he would be pleased his creation aids people even now... The Abyss has wrought enough suffering on this land. I sincerely hope this war will end soon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (No matter the cost, no matter the sacrifice... Huh, that sounds rather familiar.)
Stop worrying about other people's survival, about their losses and sacrifices. You just need to win! That must be why I've returned... for this moment.
Please finish what you've set out to do, Commander.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Hm... You're more perceptive than I imagined.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: However, some things are better kept secret for now. We may be working together, but our goals are not entirely aligned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's with the secrets all of a sudden? Paimon's starting to think we should be more careful around you!

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I do not mean to jeopardize the trust between us. I simply prefer to keep this to myself because it's a personal matter.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: All I can tell you is this — Natlan may have survived the worst of the crisis, but the souls of this land are still not at peace.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: ...And that is why my work is not yet done.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if it's personal, then we'll just have to trust you.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: If you have other questions, I'm willing to answer them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, like anything?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon wants to know how you eat with the mask... Anything you want to ask, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Actually... There is something I want to know.)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Natlan must pay the price for Mavuika's use of the Ruler of Death's power. That price is death, and only Mavuika's death can clear the debt.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Even now that the war's over and the threat to Natlan is gone, it looks like that death is still set in stone.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Could The Captain know something about the Ruler of Death? I might not get this opportunity again. I should ask him.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Ask about the Ruler of Death.)

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: In the garden cultivated by the gods, flowers and weeds grow side by side. When the weeds compete for nutrients in the soil, the gardener intervenes to inhibit their growth.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: I'm not one to pass judgment based on my own standard of right and wrong. But, it is an undeniable fact that she is responsible for my suffering, as well as that of my people.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: If that explanation is too difficult to understand, allow me to show you exactly what I mean.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: The Ruler of Death can freely define the form of death, or grant immortality to anyone she desires.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Her power is a rule in and of itself. Faced with such an overwhelming level of power, it can feel hopeless to resist.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: But, I am of the belief that, in this world, no destiny is unchangeable, no death inevitable, and no rule unbreakable.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: ...So, before the final moment truly arrives, we must fight harder than ever.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}! Paimon!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Sorry, hope I didn't interrupt anything.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: After helping Ocotlan back home, I went on a small walk, and happened to run into a messenger from the Scions of the Canopy. He's been looking for you everywhere.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, did something happen?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Apparently, Xilonen's ready to start forging your Ancient Name. She needs to check the progress of your Pilgrim's Chronicle... that device she gave you before.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: She invited a bunch of people to be there, including me. So, let's head to the Stadium once you're done here.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: #This is a critical time for you, {NICKNAME}. It's best not to delay, so let us end our conversation for now.

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: Best of luck to you all. Goodbye.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: What a mysterious guy... Still, he doesn't seem quite as intimidating as before. We're basically comrades now, right?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Anyway, let's head to the Stadium. We shouldn't keep everyone waiting.

choices.text: I don't know what I expected, but this is...
Why don't you want to use your name from five hundred years ago?

response.speaker: "The Captain"
response.text: It may seem difficult to understand, but the reason is really quite simple.

talks.objective: Go to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Sure took your sweet time...

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Wretched scoundrels! How dare you keep the Almighty Dragonlord K'uhul Ajaw waiting! Kneel before us and apologize, or we'll—

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Don't listen to him. We just got here, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich, Kachina, Mualani! Whoa... everyone's here!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Reunited at last! Did you miss us?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I brought candy and cookies to share!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course we missed you! Ooh... you brought Saurus Crackers, too? Score!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Just in time, {NICKNAME}. It's so stifling in here, I was just about to go outside to get some air.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It's the same temperature outside... Anyway, how was the trip here?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: To be honest, I also didn't expect this many people to show up.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: A third of this amount is more than enough for my plan.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why do you need them here?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I need to ask them about you, gather their thoughts and hopes. That will help the formation of your Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You brought the Pilgrim's Chronicle, right? Yeah, let me take a look.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hm... Okay, the progress looks good. We have enough people, so let's get started.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Sorry I'm late.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Chasca showing up late for something? That's a first!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I had to follow a group of monsters further than expected.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: When I got back, I heard about what you did for my tribe. Thank you.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: #Haha, {NICKNAME} deserves most of the credit.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Plus, if it weren't for your help during the battle, the Collective of Plenty would have suffered a lot more. We had the manpower to spare, so it's only right we return the favor.

choices.text: We were just doing our part.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: *ahem* Okay, let's save the pleasantries for later. Everyone's here, so let's get started.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #Alright, let me remind everyone what's going to happen. I need each of you to stand before the Pilgrim's Chronicle and share your stories about {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #Your words will be recorded and become part of {NICKNAME}'s Ancient Name. Any questions?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Nope!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Alright, then to start things off...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hold on! Remember what we discussed?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Ah, right. I almost forgot.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you can't be here for this part.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But, why? We wanna hear what everyone has to say!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I need people's true thoughts and feelings. It's best if the subject in question isn't involved.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's much more difficult to express those feelings to someone's face. People get shy in those situations, it's just how it is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You're right... Just like when Paimon doesn't have enough Mora to pay for her meal, but she's too embarrassed to tell {NICKNAME}, so she has to make up some excuse...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon... I don't think that's the same.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *ahem* So, basically, you want us to leave the Pilgrim's Chronicle here, and wait nearby?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Don't worry. This shouldn't take long.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Everything Xilonen said made sense, but did you see Citlali's reaction back there? She was definitely the one who decided we should leave.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... But staying out here is just making Paimon even more curious about what everyone's gonna say!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, you're gonna have an Ancient Name soon! Ooh, that's so exciting! Feels like we've been in Natlan for quite a while already, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've been traveling together for even longer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right! If only Paimon could say a few things about you in there...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Well, looks like you're about to have that chance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xilonen? Is everything all set?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #Almost... We're just missing one last thing. You've been by {NICKNAME}'s side the longest, Paimon. We need to hear what you have to say.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, Paimon's not from Natlan...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #It doesn't matter. As {NICKNAME}'s companion, your contributions are extremely important. You're the perfect person to finish the story.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #Sorry, {NICKNAME}. I just need to borrow Paimon for a second. It should be quick.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Despite Xilonen's assurance, quite a lot of time seems to pass.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Phew...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Paimon gave us a lot, and I mean a lot, of information... I'm not even sure the Lord of the Night managed to get all of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Well, we've been to six nations already!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Here, you can have the Pilgrim's Chronicle back. I'll need it when I forge the name, but you can continue your adventures in the meantime.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: When the time comes... I will forge you an Ancient Name unlike anything that's come before, so that you, Mavuika, and Natlan as a whole can finally put an end to this endless war.

dialogues.speaker: Ohtli
dialogues.text: Nice to see you, friend. Thanks for coming to help again.

dialogues.speaker: Yopia
dialogues.text: No thanks necessary! Wanna grab a drink tonight?

dialogues.speaker: Ohtli
dialogues.text: On any other day, I would, but... Something's going on with the tribe, and it's kinda keeping me up at night.

dialogues.speaker: Yopia
dialogues.text: Don't worry! I'm sure Coach Iansan will figure out what to do. I've never seen a problem she can't handle!

dialogues.speaker: Bahati
dialogues.text: #Whoa! Are you {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure are! You know us?

dialogues.speaker: Bahati
dialogues.text: Everyone in Natlan does! I heard you're gonna fight alongside the Pyro Archon in the final battle... Good luck!

dialogues.speaker: Yareche
dialogues.text: Stupid Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Yareche
dialogues.text: This shouldn't have happened to Cochitta... Her younger brother must be devastated.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: We made it, Chief.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: #You're here, Iansan! Oh, and you must be {NICKNAME} and Paimon. I've heard a lot about you. I'm sure we'll have a much better time now with your help.

dialogues.speaker: Munay
dialogues.text: It's alright, my boy. Papa's here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, we haven't seen Chasca around here. Where is she?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: She's busy clearing out the remaining monsters and tracking down missing warriors.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: She was the one who brought Atoco back from the wilderness. Many warriors are still out there unconscious or injured, unable to make it back to the tribe. With Chasca's help, we can prevent a lot of unnecessary deaths.

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: I'm... drowning...

dialogues.speaker: Izcalli
dialogues.text: If only Duarte was still alive...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (No reaction from Atoco... Maybe this saurian is too much of a far cry from his friend.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Based on what Izcalli told us, we need to find a Qucusaur.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back... How are you feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Duarte...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Step forward)

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: How... How did you get here? Are you here to save me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's working!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Shhh...!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: What now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Tap his head with your claw)

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Wait! Not so hard...

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Ah, that hurt... Duarte, you have to get out of here! There's something in the water!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That didn't work...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Push him lightly from behind)

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Ah, you're going to carry me out of here, just like last time.

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Over a decade later, and you're still trying to save me. I can't believe you made it this deep underwater, but I'm so glad you found me...

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Once we're out of here, let's split a huge portion of Blazed Meat Stew, just like old times! I owe you for this...

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: We're almost at the surface... People tried to tell me you were dead, you know. Hah, as if I'd let that happen. I promised to protect you. There's no way... no way...

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Wait, the battle! What happened? Did we beat that giant Abyss monster?

dialogues.speaker: Izcalli
dialogues.text: Hey, don't worry, we won.

dialogues.speaker: Atoco
dialogues.text: Phew... Thank goodness.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Be careful out there. I expect you all to come back safe, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Cuallee
dialogues.text: I'll fight by your side until every last monster is gone!

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: That's very brave of you. But, you know what would make me even happier? If this whole war would end tomorrow, so you would never have to fight at all.

dialogues.speaker: Izcalli
dialogues.text: Atoco, my friend... Hang in there. I know you can get through this.

dialogues.speaker: Cochitta
dialogues.text: The world is spinning, the mountains are parting. There are eyes, countless eyes... always watching... always staring. They're going to get me... consume me...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'll need the Pilgrim's Chronicle back when I'm ready to forge the name. If there are still adventures you want to record, better finish them before then.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I hope everything will go well... I swear, even I'm starting to feel nervous now.

dialogues.speaker: Bahati
dialogues.text: Cochitta is getting better, too!

dialogues.speaker: Yareche
dialogues.text: So all those rumors about the Traveler really are true...

dialogues.speaker: Abundi
dialogues.text: How's Ocotlan doing?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Chuychu, give me a hand for a sec—... Ah, right. Chuychu's not... She's not... here anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a few days since the battle. Hopefully the tribes are getting back to normal...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Flower-Feather Clan was hit the hardest, right? That's Chasca's tribe. Maybe we should check how everyone's doing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We might be able to help them out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, isn't that Iansan? Wonder what she's doing here...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Let's see... One of those guys was talking about being cold. Do you still remember him?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: It's not often that you see someone almost drown on dry land... Let's go talk to him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Found one! Now, we just need to borrow its identity.)

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Seems like the key to getting through to them is whatever they cherish the most.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Kind of like their last spark of hope... Now we know how to help the others!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Let's take heart from this, and keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Bahati
dialogues.text: Cochitta is getting better, too!

dialogues.speaker: Yareche
dialogues.text: So all those rumors about the Traveler really are true...

dialogues.speaker: Abundi
dialogues.text: How's Ocotlan doing?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Chuychu, give me a hand for a sec—... Ah, right. Chuychu's not... She's not... here anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, in the end, The Captain still hasn't told us his real goal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He kind of reminds Paimon of someone we met recently... Oh, right! The Lord of the Night!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They just seem so... tired, you know? Since they've both been alive for many centuries, do you think that's just what happens when you've been alive for too long...?
